title: AdapterDescriptor
description: v0.7 (Ledger T4a, AC-8) adds the optional `protocol_version` integer — the adapter-contract version this descriptor's adapter implements (1 = pre-Ledger-T4a shape, 2 = poll/resolve_webhook/cancel take ctx and cache no client on self). Optional here (unlike the pydantic AdapterDescriptor model, which requires it with no default) so this schema stays additive over v0.6: a v0.6 descriptor — in this repo or a third party's — remains valid without a code change on the wire-format side; the pydantic model is what actually enforces every in-process adapter registration declares it by name (AC-8's own registration-time requirement lives in router/registry.py's Registry.register(), not in this schema).

capabilities.description: each value: 'verified' | 'claimed' | false. verified = live-run/benchmark; claimed = vendor doc only.

channels.description: per response channel: 'N' native | 'D' derivable | 'X' impossible (matrix grades, normalized_schema.md §4)

block_granularity.description: Optional hint: the native granularity of this backend's blocks so consumers and compare can reason about packaging differences instead of discovering them empirically (§4.3).

credentials_spec.description: v0.2 — secrets/credentials the adapter reads from ctx.credentials.values. The env broker resolves each from `env` in precedence order.

config_spec.description: v0.2 — non-secret config the adapter reads from ctx.runtime (endpoint, model, processor id, region).

signup_url.description: v0.2 — where a user provisions credentials for this backend.

accepts_url.description: v0.2 — backend natively ingests document.url (else the caller downloads it first).

live_gate_env.description: v0.2 — env vars whose presence gates the live test (explicit for ambient-chain backends).

batch.description: v0.4 — native batch intake. Absent => platform batching (the runner fans out single-document runs). Present with native truthy => the adapter accepts a whole item list via submit_many/normalize_many.

native.description: Grade of native multi-document submission. false (or absent) => platform batching only.

max_concurrency.description: Platform-batching concurrency cap when native is false (e.g. CPU-bound locals).

liveness.description: v0.5 — liveness-probe declaration. Absent (or probe='none') => this backend implements no liveness probe, and the platform infers a status from configuration instead (configured_unverified / not_configured). Present with probe != 'none' => the adapter implements the optional LivenessProbeAdapter method and it may be called. Statically readable with no call, so a UI can say 'cannot be tested' — or 'checking this leaves your network' — before probing anything.

probe.description: What performing the probe actually does. 'none' (default) = no probe. 'local' = in-process/subprocess, no network. 'endpoint' = network, to infrastructure the CALLER operates (self-hosted container / model server) — does not leave their network. 'vendor' = network, to a third party — it does, and may count against a rate limit. A probe is NEVER a billed request in any kind: a vendor with no free liveness call declares 'none' and takes the inferred status instead.

method.description: What the probe does, for humans and logs: 'GET /health', 'GET /v1/models', 'import fitz'.

timeout_s.description: The adapter's own recommended bound. The caller still applies its own ceiling.

notes.description: Caveats worth stating: rate-limit interaction, cold-start behaviour, what a healthy answer proves.

idempotency_supported.description: v0.6 (BL-166) — true iff this adapter forwards a caller/OpenReading-supplied idempotency key to the vendor in a form the vendor actually honors on a retried submit. false is an honest declaration for a vendor with no such mechanism — OpenReading never invents a token the vendor would silently ignore.

cancel_supported.description: v0.6 (BL-164) — true iff this adapter's cancel() actually stops the job at the vendor, not merely locally. false is an honest declaration so `on_win: cancel` prices its effect truthfully instead of implying a stop it cannot produce.

protocol_version.description: v0.7 (Ledger T4a, AC-8) — the adapter-contract version this descriptor's adapter implements. 1 = pre-Ledger-T4a shape (poll/resolve_webhook/cancel take no ctx; an adapter MAY cache a client on self). 2 = Ledger T4a shape (poll/resolve_webhook/cancel take ctx: RunContext; no built-in client is ever cached on self). Not in `required` here — this schema stays additive over v0.6 — but the pydantic AdapterDescriptor model requires it with no default, and router/registry.py's Registry.register() refuses to register a descriptor declaring a version below the router's own current floor.
